common_name: Skylark Rose (Coral-Orange Semi-Double David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Skylark bears semi-double, coral-orange flowers with a lighter reverse on a vigorous, well-branched shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Skylark bears semi-double flowers in warm coral-orange with a lighter, almost apricot reverse, showing prominent golden stamens at the open center, a slightly more informal and pollinator-friendly flower form than the densely double blooms typical of the English rose line. It carries a light, fresh fragrance and reblooms reliably in flushes from late spring through fall on a vigorous, well-branched shrub. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Susan Williams-Ellis Rose (Pure White David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Susan Williams-Ellis bears pure white, rosette-shaped blooms on a compact, disease-resistant shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Susan Williams-Ellis bears fully double, rosette-shaped blooms in pure white with a light, sweet fragrance, opening on a compact, well-branched shrub bred with the improved disease resistance characteristic of more recent David Austin introductions. Its clean white color works easily into nearly any color scheme, pairing well with pastels or bold companions alike. It reblooms generously from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Lichfield Angel Rose (Ivory-White with Peach Center David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Lichfield Angel bears ivory-white blooms warmed with a soft peachy-buff center on a compact, disease-resistant shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Named for a stained-glass angel window in Lichfield Cathedral, this rose bears semi-double to double blooms in soft ivory-white warmed by a gentle peachy-buff glow at the center, with a light, fresh fragrance, opening on a compact, well-branched shrub bred with good disease resistance. Its gentle, luminous coloring works beautifully in romantic, cottage-style plantings. It reblooms reliably from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: The Ancient Mariner Rose (Tall Soft Pink David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; The Ancient Mariner grows notably tall for an Austin rose and can be used as a large shrub or short climber.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, providing support if trained as a short climber. The Ancient Mariner bears large, cupped, soft pink double blooms with a strong, fruity fragrance on unusually tall, vigorous canes for an English rose, tall enough to be trained against a fence or pillar as well as grown as a large freestanding shrub. It reblooms generously from late spring through fall. Prune to control size and shape in late winter — lightly if grown as a shrub, or by thinning old wood if trained as a climber — and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Imogen Rose (Pale Yellow-Green Tinted David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Imogen bears pale yellow flowers with a distinctive greenish tint at the center.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Imogen bears rosette-shaped blooms in pale primrose-yellow with an unusual soft greenish tint deepening toward the flower center, a subtle, cool coloring distinct from the warmer yellows more common in the English rose line, carrying a light, fresh fragrance. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall on a compact, well-branched shrub that fits smaller beds and mixed borders. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive
